what_it_does: This paper describes a wireless power transmitter—the kind of circuit that charges your phone or smartwatch without a cable. The challenge is that wireless power efficiency drops dramatically when the device being charged changes its power requirements or distance. Traditional designs are tuned for one specific scenario and lose efficiency once the load shifts. This design solves that problem by adapting on the fly: it monitors both the strength and phase of the signal and dynamically adjusts the matching network (the impedance-matching components that couple power from transmitter to receiver). This dual adaptation—adjusting for both real and imaginary electrical properties—maintains 94.2% efficiency across a wide range of charging scenarios, and successfully powered a 33-watt system.
